summary: The bounded correction review confirms resolution of both original deployment-script findings at the current plan digests. Backup invocations now acquire one installation lock before state inspection and retain it through final writer restart; initialization rejects permissive or foreign-owned installation/configuration directories before creating secrets, and preflight checks matching directory ownership/modes. No supported remaining finding was identified in this correction scope.
coverage: Read correction-brief.txt (SHA-256 5ea86a3d7361ab8b2aca507beb8afa12831557a07b6959dd7a2f7abdf4f3aa70), the updated plan and its preserved original-review snapshot. Verified all assigned current file hashes: {"Dockerfile": "ac72e727e331af0cff014d4681c78aba382d84a0e8b6d47947df495ace6d9c9f", "apps/server/src/auth/config.ts": "209c74005e490d18393ecd71f51ac84914f8b345ebcfb7a5615f9eacf70da2f7", "apps/server/src/blobs/index.ts": "f21034309a3d42c75976c9bd5ca1baa526cfa42eff40b71c7cc5aa0ba924f1d5", "apps/server/src/context.ts": "175b33033c0b5e8d043daf3e88d829c5e9aa8f1b190d1f4dc59a3e318a0bf757", "deploy/reactor/backup.py": "9d46d184cd25da150ac61b8400677cc11fd42e7f70a144aaeeae8b0d8f13c018", "deploy/reactor/compose.yaml": "af7bcf79c05edef725f529268fab7350a4ba5687ecd9d7f96170867310448a6c", "deploy/reactor/initialize.py": "ae07c2804140a5fcf3a1979f8439267c17aaf75fd9a493c72e9a1f54b9302c28", "deploy/reactor/preflight.py": "059945aa0d0278060af2c6e30ceb44c0304aafd6beb250dae91e16d7be6a9494"}

Inspected backup.py:16-22 and 38-75: exclusive nonblocking flock is acquired before Docker state checks, and the raw descriptor is retained by the script through capture and finally restart; normal process exit releases it.

Inspected initialize.py:11-22 and 49-52: root/shared must be owned by the effective UID with exact mode 0700 before generating or writing credentials, and shared symlinks are rejected. Container-readable credential files remain protected by the private host directory.
Inspected preflight.py:23-28: the report rejects nonprivate or foreign-owned root/shared directories in addition to requiring app.env mode 0600.

Inspected verify-packaging.py (SHA-256 1f1cffa019ba33e9edf17f37d6daa96d8fb320b67ce23a1d0d940e08bb28a53e) and packaging-verification.json (SHA-256 dc605688adb652f720ddf4a0ad637f838753c90b36e44be3366e10107955da0e). The lead reports six passing tempfile/mocked-Docker checks covering permissive-directory rejection, credential replacement, staging/identity separation, lock contention, archive/config capture and final restart on dump failure. These are inspected lead results, not claimed as independently rerun.

Executed an additional isolated tempfile/mock check against unmodified current backup.py. Every mocked Docker call attempted a second independent open/flock of backup.lock and observed contention, including the final up command. Observed command sequence ps, stop, exec, exec, run, up and a complete receipt. No real Docker subprocess was invoked.
Executed an additional isolated tempfile check against current initialize.py with shared explicitly 0755. It rejected the directory with the 0700 requirement and wrote no secrets.
All three deployment scripts parsed with ast.parse. Original review.json and result.json hashes were checked unchanged.
limitations: This is a follow-up correction pass with inherited knowledge of the two original findings, not a fresh application-security assessment or a complete repeat of the original infrastructure review.

No SSH, Docker, live service, live credentials, real backup/archive, restoration, application-integrity or off-host retention validation was executed. Mock command results establish script coordination only.

Locking serializes cooperating backup.py invocations. Writer quiescence still assumes no external app/database/artifact writer and no operator removal/replacement of the lock file; abrupt process/host failure is not a completed restart or recovery drill.
Correct directory ownership/modes were evaluated locally and by source; actual target permissions were not independently inspected in this pass. No current exposed-credential claim is made.
Package/base-image advisories, prior application findings, provider login, bootstrap ownership, public HTTPS, capacity and live-user admission remain outside this correction scope.
